properties.headline: Freeze Watch issued October 22 at 8:59PM PDT until October 24 at 9:00AM PDT by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Frost Advisory, temperatures as low of 33 to 36
degrees will result in frost formation. For the Freeze Watch,
sub-freezing temperatures possible.

* WHERE...East Central Willamette Valley, North Oregon Coast Range,
West Central Willamette Valley, Cascade Foothills of Marion and
Linn Counties, and Lane County Cascade Foothills.

* WHEN...For the Frost Advisory, until 9 AM PDT Friday. For the
Freeze Watch, from Friday evening through Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing. Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.
properties.instruction:
Take steps now to protect tender outdoor plants from the cold.
Consider temporarily moving outdoor potted plants indoors if they are
sensitive to cold temperatures, or temporarily covering sensitive
plants with a lightweight cotton fabric (i.e., bedsheets, thin
blankets), as this will help retain heat and provide frost protection
for your plants.

properties.areaDesc: Catron, NM
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 22 at 9:57PM MDT until October 23 at 2:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Catron County in west central New Mexico...

* Until 200 AM MDT.

* At 957 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 1.25 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Gila Cliff Dwellings and Beaverhead.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.areaDesc: Grant, NM
properties.senderName: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 22 at 9:57PM MDT until October 22 at 10:30PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
SVREPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
North central Grant County in southwestern New Mexico...

* Until 1030 PM MDT.

* At 957 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Gila, moving
northeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage
to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Riverside, Gila, Mogollon Box Day Use Area, and Portions of the
Gila Wilderness.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall across the area is
occurring.

* WHERE...South Central La Plata County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 948 PM MDT, Gauge reports the La Plata River has risen above
flood stage due to heavy rain. Flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly in the warned area. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of
rain have fallen across the area over the past two days.
- This includes the La Plata River and the surrounding low areas
near the river.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hesperus.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 9:52PM MDT until October 23 at 10:45AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
Dangerous flooding of rivers, creeks and streams will be possible
into early Friday morning due to continuous moderate to heavy rain.
If flood waters threaten, climb to higher ground immediately.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Western Conejos County in south central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 1045 AM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from continuing rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 944 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. Flooding is already occurring in the warned area.
Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are possible in
the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Conejos River, La Jara Creek and Alamosa River and their
tributaries.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following

Canyonlands/Natural Bridges, La Sal and Abajo Mountains and

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 22 at 9:29PM MDT until October 23 at 12:30AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Grant County in southwestern New Mexico...

* Until 1230 AM MDT.

* At 929 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain
has fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
San Lorenzo, Hurley, Cobre, Bayard, Mimbres, Hanover, North Hurley,
Santa Clara, Shingle Canyon, Bear Canyon, Allie Canyon and Soldiers
Canyon.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.
